{{for|other Milnor conjectures|Milnor conjecture (disambiguation)}}
In 1968 [[John Milnor]] conjectured<ref name=Milnor_1968/> that the [[fundamental group]] of a [[geodesic manifold|complete manifold]] is [[Finitely generated group|finitely generated]] if its [[Ricci curvature]] stays nonnegative. In an oversimplified interpretation, such a manifold has a finite number of "[[Hole (topology)|holes]]". A version for [[Almost flat manifold|almost-flat manifolds]] holds from work of [[Mikhael Gromov (mathematician)|Gromov]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gromov |first=M. |date=1978-01-01 |title=Almost flat manifolds |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/journal-of-differential-geometry/volume-13/issue-2/Almost-flat-manifolds/10.4310/jdg/1214434488.full |journal=Journal of Differential Geometry |volume=13 |issue=2 |doi=10.4310/jdg/1214434488 |issn=0022-040X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=Cepelewicz_2024/>

In two dimensions <math>M^2</math> has finitely generated fundamental group as a consequence that if  <math>\operatorname{Ric}>0</math> for noncompact <math>M^2</math>, then it is [[Flat manifold|flat]] or [[diffeomorphic]] to <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math>, by work of [[Stefan Cohn-Vossen|Cohn-Vossen]] from 1935.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cohn-Vossen |first=Stefan |date=1935 |title=Kürzeste Wege und Totalkrümmung auf Flächen |url=https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1935__2__69_0/ |journal=Compositio Mathematica |language=en |volume=2 |pages=69–133 |issn=1570-5846}}</ref><ref name=2303.15347/>

In three dimensions the conjecture holds due to a noncompact <math>M^3</math> with <math>\operatorname{Ric}>0</math> being diffeomorphic to <math>\mathbb{R}^3</math> or having its [[universal cover]] [[isometry|isometrically]] split. The diffeomorphic part is due to [[Richard Schoen|Schoen]]-[[Shing-Tung Yau|Yau]] (1982)<ref>{{Citation |last1=Schoen |first1=Richard |chapter=Complete Three Dimensional Manifolds with Positive Ricci Curvature and Scalar Curvature |date=1982-12-31 |title=Seminar on Differential Geometry. (AM-102) |pages=209–228 |editor-last=Yau |editor-first=Shing-tung |chapter-url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/9781400881918-013/html |access-date=2024-05-24 |publisher=Princeton University Press |doi=10.1515/9781400881918-013 |isbn=978-1-4008-8191-8 |last2=Yau |first2=Shing-Tung|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=2303.15347/> while the other part is by Liu (2013).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Liu |first=Gang |date=August 2013 |title=3-Manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00222-012-0428-x |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=193 |issue=2 |pages=367–375 |doi=10.1007/s00222-012-0428-x |issn=0020-9910|arxiv=1108.1888 |bibcode=2013InMat.193..367L }}</ref><ref name=2303.15347/> Another proof of the full statement has been given by Pan (2020).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pan |first=Jiayin |date=2020 |title=A proof of Milnor conjecture in dimension 3 |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik |language=en |volume=2020 |issue=758 |pages=253–260 |doi=10.1515/crelle-2017-0057 |issn=1435-5345|arxiv=1703.08143 }}</ref><ref name=2303.15347/>

In 2023 Bruè, [[Aaron Naber|Naber]] and Semola disproved in two preprints the conjecture for six<ref name=2311.12155/> or more<ref name=2303.15347/> dimensions by constructing [[counterexample]]s that they described as "smooth fractal snowflakes". The status of the conjecture for four or five dimensions remains open.<ref name=Cepelewicz_2024/>
